peer_results.rationale: Although AMD also reports an 'All Other' segment, its disclosure focuses on the specific financial composition of the operating loss (amortization and stock-based compensation) rather than the structural definition of the segment's constituent businesses or entities as provided by Intel. The topics are related but distinct: one is structural composition, the other is expense driver analysis.

AVGO's disclosures focus on reportable segment definitions (Semiconductor Solutions, Infrastructure Software) and cash flow impacts from VMware. There is no disclosure of a specific 'All Other' segment category comparable to Intel's definition of non-reportable segments like Altera and Mobileye.
MU's Item 7 candidates discuss critical accounting estimates and dividend policies. There is no disclosure of an 'All Other' segment or comparable non-reportable segment results.

comparisons.peer_summary: The year-on-year decrease in All Other operating loss was attributed to the absence of the $1.4 billion Arm acquisition termination cost incurred in fiscal year 2023, partially offset by an $839 million increase in stock-based compensation expense in fiscal year 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and NVIDIA disclose the composition and drivers of their 'All Other' segment results. Intel defines 'All Other' to include non-reportable segments like Altera and Mobileye, as well as start-ups and divested business results. NVIDIA reports an 'All Other' operating loss, attributing its year-on-year change primarily to the absence of a $1.4 billion acquisition termination cost in the prior year, while also noting increases in stock-based compensation. While Intel focuses on the structural composition of the segment (entities included), NVIDIA focuses on the variance drivers (costs incurred) within that same reporting category.

sentences.text: Our "all other" category includes the results of operations from other non-reportable segments not otherwise presented, including our Altera and Mobileye businesses, start-up businesses that support our initiatives, and historical results of operations from divested businesses.

All Other operating loss - The year-on-year decrease was due to the $1.4 billion Arm acquisition termination cost in fiscal year 2023, partially offset by a $839 million increase in stock-based compensation expense in fiscal year 2024.
